svg.title: This paper develops quantum-source constructions within Shadow Theory’s pre-existing source–readout programme [13]. The stationary classical completion used for comparison is established in Rodgers [12]. An observed stochastic law may admit several source realizations with different internal memories and different retained-output costs. We study these resources separately for stationary quantum instruments, emphasizing the delayed trine law. The results combine a general positive-semidefinite factorization completion theorem, exact memory regimes and a two-objective memory/environment frontier with a constructive mixed-support source. For 0 ≤λ ≤1, put Tii = λ/3 and Tij = (3 −λ)/6 for i ̸= j. The target has uniform adjacent pairs and full word law P(y1 · · · yn) = 9−1 ∏︁n−2 t=1 Tyt,yt+2. It is the interleaving of two independent stationary chains. A source consists of a stationary density matrix and time-homogeneous CP symbol maps whose sum is trace preserving. The emitted trit is retained in an append-only classical archive; archive feedback, correlated future tapes and uncounted returning controllers are excluded. All history-correlated systems accessible to future operations belong to the reusable causal memory.
